unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision deletes the critic's retort that the family's success came from the field Europe gave them. That retort is what the next sentence's 'more timid ... for their children than for themselves' contrasts against. The father's anti-Europe rule now stands unironized.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The irony against Henry's respectability, which the plan treats as essential, survives intact.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's critic sentence and its 'But' connective.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: The essential item covers the parents' fear only; this irony is a planning omission.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The opening's double irony against both father and son is halved. The 'themselves' comparison reads as a generic truism rather than a jab at Adamses who rose through Europe, and it also loses the setup for the London Legation.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Captious-critic irony cut; 'than for themselves' loses its contrast

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision removes 'Thus far it had remained in the eighteenth century, and the next step took it back to the sixteenth.' The paragraph now jumps from the chiasmus straight to 'He crossed to Antwerp', so the announced backward movement has no stated mechanism.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'London of the eighteenth century' and 'middle ages and the sixteenth century alive' survive, so an attentive reader can reconstruct the step.

evidence.quote: Thus far it had remained in the eighteenth century, and the next step took it back to the sixteenth. He crossed to Antwerp.
Thus far it had remained in the eighteenth century, and the next step took it back to the sixteenth.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the one sentence (20 words) before 'He crossed to Antwerp.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Supports the essential item 'London as an insolent eighteenth-century city ... Antwerp as purely sensual, mediaeval education'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The sequence London (eighteenth century), then Antwerp (sixteenth/mediaeval) is the chapter's comic logic of regression. Without it, 'Education went backward' reads as merely figurative.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'Education went backward' loses its 18th-to-16th-century step

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft cut 'Mere mechanical repetition ... stuck to his unconscious mind', which grounds 'this power'. The revision then cut 'read a new language' and the flower sentence ('accidental, and not to be trusted'). The prison-wall image now leads straight to 'slowly came to admit'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: V6, the 'overrated' joke and 'never so much as listened' all survive, so the episode remains intelligible.

evidence.quote: He could not have been more astonished had he suddenly read a new language.
A new sense burst out like a flower in his life, so bewildering that he could not credit it, and watched it as something apart, accidental, and not to be trusted.
without so much as his knowing when it happened. He slowly came to admit that Beethoven had partly become intelligible to him

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'astonished ... new language' and flower sentences. Optionally add 'Mere mechanical repetition of certain sounds had stuck to his unconscious mind.'
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The young man's suspicion of the new sense is what sets up the comic conclusion that Beethoven 'must be much overrated'. Losing it, along with the language-struggle echo, makes the episode abrupt and leaves 'this power' vague.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Beethoven awakening stripped of its astonishment and distrust
